thread:
pagerduty-bot: :rotating_light: INCIDENT detected: Multiple serve pods in us-west-2 hitting EphemeralStorage > 95%, causing evictions and subsequent container restarts. Auto-pager sent to oncall.

maria (oncall): I'm on it, joining. Observed p99 latency spikes concurrent with restarts. Any customer impact flagged?

sara (support): Customer impact: a handful of requests returned 5xx from a mid-market customer for ~10m ago, came through support queue. No SLO bleed yet but degraded throughput.

maria (oncall): quick checks — listing pods in serving pool.
```bash
kubectl get pods -n serve -o wide | grep us-west
```

maria (oncall): Found 3 pods in CrashLoopBackOff and 2 recently evicted. Node disk usage shows /var/lib/kubelet/pods at 98%.

raj (eng-runtime): Likely model-cache/ckpt writes filling ephemeral. We had a recent change to the checkpoint TTL handler last week. Could be leaking files with no expiry.

kevin (eng-sre): Can you dump largest files on one of the affected nodes? I'll cordon if needed.

maria (oncall): Running du:
```bash
ssh node-uw2-12
sudo du -sh /var/lib/* | sort -h | tail -n 20
# showed /var/lib/model_cache/checkpoints = 1.7T
ls -lh /var/lib/model_cache/checkpoints | head
```

maria (oncall): There are dozens of checkpoint blobs named like chk-write-ttl-20260301-<uuid>.bin, timestamps spanning months. Many have .ttl marker files but their timestamps are stale.

raj (eng-runtime): That matches a bug where the TTL reaper thread silently exited if it encountered an unexpected permission error. The writer keeps appending checkpoints; reaper didn't remove old ones. That leads to runaway disk use and then kernel evict.

kevin (eng-sre): Imminent plan: 1) stop checkpoint-writer on affected nodes 2) delete safe-to-remove oldest checkpoints 3) restart pods gracefully 4) set temporary admission limit for preloading. I'll coordinate.

maria (oncall): I'm pausing new canary deployments and setting autoscaler min replicas to avoid churn.

ops-bot: Command executed: `kubectl cordon node-uw2-12` (user: kevin)

kevin (eng-sre): On node-uw2-12 now. Stopping checkpoint-writer: `systemctl stop checkpoint-writer || pkill -f checkpoint-writer`

raj (eng-runtime): Dump of recent pod logs shows CUDA failures on restart:
```
2026-03-01T12:43:10Z RuntimeError: CUDA out of memory. Tried to allocate 2.04 GiB (GPU 0; 14.73 GiB total capacity; 12.34 GiB already allocated)
[...]
E CudaDriver failure: out of memory
```

maria (oncall): So what's happening: eviction frees disk, pods restart quicker, runtime preloads models which then OOM on GPU because model cache got partially corrupted and the runtime tries to rehydrate large KV caches. Confirm?

raj (eng-runtime): Yup. The runtime's preloader grabs model shards into GPU memory after process start. If disk I/O is slow/corrupt it can cause partial loads and inconsistent memory accounting — leads to OOM. Workaround: disable preloading and fallback to smaller model variant while we cleanup.

kevin (eng-sre): I'm moving to delete stale checkpoints older than 30 days on node-uw2-12: `find /var/lib/model_cache/checkpoints -type f -mtime +30 -print0 | xargs -0 -n 50 rm -f` — doing dry-run first.

maria (oncall): Please annotate which files removed for audit. Use `sha256sum` list before deletion.

kevin (eng-sre): Doing that now. Outputting to s3://rwd-incident-logs/3723456789/node-uw2-12-checkpoints.txt

ops-bot: Upload success to s3.

kevin (eng-sre): Deleted ~1.1T of old checkpoint blobs. Re-ran `df -h` — node free space back to 40%.

maria (oncall): Great. Now restarting pods one at a time with prefetch disabled.

raj (eng-runtime): Patch to runtime: set env REDWOOD_PRELOAD=false and MODEL_VARIANT=compact for serve pods. Applying to namespace serve with rollout pause between pods.

maria (oncall): Applied. Rolling restart initiated.

sara (support): Noted: customer error rate returned to baseline after first restarted pod completed warmup. Marking customer impact as mitigated.

tim (customer-ops): Thanks, please confirm if we should notify affected customer about root cause and remediation steps.

maria (oncall): We'll prepare a short postmortem and a customer-facing note. Capture timeline and ETA for permanent fix.

kevin (eng-sre): Follow-ups for postmortem: - reintroduce TTL reaper robustly; add health-check restart if reaper exits - instrument checkpoint-writer to emit retention metrics - add eviction-resistant compaction job to cap on-disk cache - alert when model_cache dir > 70% for nodal threshold

raj (eng-runtime): Runtime follow-ups: - avoid eager GPU preloading on restarts if disk pressure detected - add atomic checkpoint commit + reservation to avoid partial corrupt loads - runtime should detect partially written blobs and skip them gracefully

maria (oncall): Handoff: I'm stepping off rotation in 10m. Handing to kevin for follow-ups and cleanup validation. kevin, you OK to take on-call?

kevin (eng-sre): Taking it. I'll schedule the postmortem and run through remediation checklist.

maria (oncall): Thanks team. Final notes: temporary mitigation applied, customer impact mitigated, root cause appears to be TTL reaper exit causing orphaned checkpoint buildup -> disk pressure -> pod eviction -> runtime restart + preloader -> GPU OOMs. We'll keep this thread for the postmortem links and docs.

pagerduty-bot: Incident resolved: node-uw2-12 freed and pods stabilized. Incident closed at 3723457089 (automated).

kevin (eng-sre): I'll attach logs and the sha256 manifest to the postmortem doc and ping product for customer communication drafts.

maria (oncall): handing over. :white_check_mark:
